title: Why a vLLM prefix hit saves tokens but still takes KV blocks
question: How do a V1 token budget and KV ownership differ when one dense-model request hits its prefix cache?
audience: Python engineer familiar with autoregressive decoding, new to vLLM
scope: One synchronous single-GPU decoder-only request; equal hash and physical block sizes; prefill and two decode inputs; no model execution
assumptions: Token IDs are constructed; no tokenizer or model output was measured.
Dense decoder-only, one full-attention cache group; hash and physical block sizes equal.
Warm cache is a completed prior request, not an in-flight producer.
Synchronous sequential steps; no eviction, connectors, encoder input, speculative tokens or fine-grained hits.
Toy pool counts model block metadata, not bytes or a measured GPU capacity.

claims.statement: The selected no-draft running branch catches computed positions up with known inputs, within compute and input budgets.
The manager caps cache-hit length at known tokens minus one; single-group whole-block alignment gives 32 of 35 or 16 of 32.
One-group coordinator passes its physical block size as hit alignment.
Full-attention lookup walks initial cached blocks and stops on a first miss.
Idle prefix hits add to admission capacity demand; allocation returns new blocks, not the full request table.
Touching a cached idle block removes it from the free queue and increments references.
Allocation registers full finalized cache metadata before later executor computation.
Computed counters advance in scheduling and are accompanied by in-flight counters.
The selected EngineCore step waits for model output before processing that output.
Appending sampled output IDs extends the all-token ID list.
